claims.claim: Woodcock calls Le Guin's a style of crystalline clarity and functional flexibility.
claims.source: George Woodcock, quoted by John R. Pfeiffer in Joe De Bolt, ed., Ursula K. Le Guin: Voyager to Inner Lands and to Outer Space (Kennikat Press, 1979)
claims.quote: a style of crystalline clarity and functional flexibility

claims.claim: Pfeiffer calls the oral elements of the style of A Wizard of Earthsea a superb vehicle.
claims.source: John R. Pfeiffer, in Joe De Bolt, ed., Ursula K. Le Guin: Voyager to Inner Lands and to Outer Space (1979)
claims.quote: The oral elements of the style of WOE

claims.claim: Dirda says Le Guin gives her prose music occasionally through the use of alliteration and assonance.
claims.source: Michael Dirda, NEA Big Read teacher's guide to A Wizard of Earthsea (2008)
claims.quote: through the use of alliteration and assonance

claims.claim: A review of Tehanu reprinted in Children's Literature Review says Le Guin's style is as pellucid as ever.
claims.source: An unsigned review of Tehanu, reprinted in Children's Literature Review vol. 28 (Gale, 1992)
claims.quote: Le Guin's style is as pellucid as ever

claims.claim: Cogell's bibliography records a review calling Le Guin's style in one book different from her preceding works.
claims.source: Elizabeth Cummins Cogell, Ursula K. Le Guin: A Primary and Secondary Bibliography (G. K. Hall, 1983)
claims.quote: Le Guin's style is different from her preceding works

claims.claim: Juliette Wade observes that the archival header opening The Left Hand of Darkness contains no verbs at all.
claims.source: Juliette Wade, 'Genly Ai: A Ridiculously Close Look', TalkToYoUniverse blog, 2008
claims.quote: Notice that there are no verbs in this excerpt

claims.claim: Wade argues that the verbless archival header removes every actor and leaves what she calls a sourceless truth.
claims.source: Juliette Wade, 'Genly Ai: A Ridiculously Close Look', TalkToYoUniverse blog, 2008
claims.quote: leaving us with a sourceless truth

claims.claim: Wade identifies the register of the novel's archival header as that of the notes heading a scientific report.
claims.source: Juliette Wade, 'Genly Ai: A Ridiculously Close Look', TalkToYoUniverse blog, 2008
claims.quote: the notes that would head a scientific report

claims.claim: Wade reads the header's dating line as showing that the institution keeps its own measurement of time.
claims.source: Juliette Wade, 'Genly Ai: A Ridiculously Close Look', TalkToYoUniverse blog, 2008
claims.quote: it also dictates its own measurement of time
claims.page: paragraph on the number of alien names

claims.claim: Wade counts three distinct voices in the opening page of The Left Hand of Darkness, of which the archival header is the second.
claims.source: Juliette Wade, 'Genly Ai: A Ridiculously Close Look', TalkToYoUniverse blog, 2008
claims.quote: This is a voice of ultimate authority

claims.claim: The Left Hand of Darkness opens with a filing header that names an archive and a document number before any sentence with a verb.
claims.source: Ursula K. Le Guin, The Left Hand of Darkness, ch. 1 opening, reproduced in Books on GIF review #280
claims.quote: From the Archives of Hain. Transcript of Ansible Document

claims.claim: Genly Ai's first sentence names the document he is writing as a report before it narrates anything.
claims.source: Ursula K. Le Guin, The Left Hand of Darkness, ch. 1 opening, reproduced in Books on GIF review #280
claims.quote: I’ll make my report as if I told a story

claims.claim: The report's opening concedes that its account is neither wholly the reporter's nor told by him alone.
claims.source: Ursula K. Le Guin, The Left Hand of Darkness, ch. 1 opening, reproduced in Books on GIF review #280
claims.quote: The story is not all mine, nor told by me alone

claims.claim: The report fixes its starting point by an ordinal day of a numbered year before naming any person or place.
claims.source: Ursula K. Le Guin, The Left Hand of Darkness, ch. 1 opening, reproduced in Books on GIF review #280
claims.quote: It starts on the 44th diurnal of the Year 1491

claims.claim: A local timekeeping custom is stated as a bare present-tense sentence of seven ordinary words.
claims.source: Ursula K. Le Guin, The Left Hand of Darkness, ch. 1 opening, reproduced in Books on GIF review #280
claims.quote: It is always the Year One here

verdicts.trueWording: Woodcock: "a style of crystalline clarity and functional flexibility"
verdicts.note: archive.org full-text of ursulakleguinvoy0000unse (De Bolt 1979) reads: Le Guin's prose style draws Woodcock's attention, then the quoted phrase, continuing 'that has always reminded me of the limpid prose...' — the 'me' inside the quotation is Woodcock, so the phrase is his. Quote contiguous and exact.

verdicts.trueWording: "oral elements of the style of WOE are a superb vehicle"
verdicts.note: Same volume: the fragment carries the running head '124 / JOHN R. PFEIFFER', so the chapter author is Pfeiffer; a separate hit in the volume's abbreviation key gives 'WOE - A Wizard of Earthsea', supporting the claim's expansion. Every limb met.

verdicts.trueWording: "gives music and richness to her prose through the rhythm"
verdicts.note: archive.org full-text of ursulakleguinswi00dird: 'She gives music and richness to her prose through the rhythm of her sentences and occasionally through the use of alliteration and assonance.' Item metadata and an internal credits page ('Writers: Michael Dirda for the National Endowment for the Arts') confirm the NEA Big Read teacher's guide (2008) is Dirda's.

verdicts.trueWording: "Le Guin's style is as pellucid as ever"
verdicts.note: childrensliterat28gera (Children's Literature Review vol. 28, 1992), p. 292: the quoted clause continues 'and her plotting as strong, but Tehanu owes its parentage not so much to Earthsea...', which fixes Tehanu as the book under review. Verbatim and on-page.

verdicts.trueWording: "Le Guin's style is different from her preceding works"
verdicts.note: Quote is verbatim in Cogell's bibliography (ursulakleguinpri0000coge), ending the annotation that runs up to the next heading, 'D618 SELTZER, HARA L. Review of ...'. The annotated item is therefore D617 SEIDEL, KATHRYN L., 'The Lathe of Heaven,' In Survey of Science Fiction Literature, ed. Frank N. Magill - a critical essay. The bibliography's own index labels D617 '[article]', and it labels genuine reviews 'Review of X' (as in D618), so the 'review' limb fails; the 'one book' limb (The Lathe of Heaven) holds.
verdicts.unsupportedLimb: 'a review' - the annotated item D617 is Seidel's essay in Magill's Survey of Science Fiction Literature, not a review

verdicts.trueWording: "Notice that there are no verbs in this excerpt"
verdicts.note: Raw HTML of the 2008-10-04 TalkToYoUniverse post fetched directly (200, 21,672 bytes); the sentence follows Wade's block quotation of the 'From the Archives of Hain...' header, which she calls the second voice. Post signed 'Posted by Juliette Wade'.
Same paragraph states that no verbs means no subjects and thus no actors, with agency, identity and intent removed, before the quoted clause - so the 'removes every actor' limb is on the page too.

verdicts.trueWording: "the notes that would head a scientific report"
verdicts.note: Same paragraph, describing the archival header: a voice of ultimate authority, then the quoted phrase, then the sense of a completely factual account. Register limb supported.

verdicts.trueWording: "it also dictates its own measurement of time"
verdicts.note: Paragraph beginning 'Think about the number of alien names in these few sentences': Wade reads the header as an overarching institutional structure that spans planets and, in the quoted clause, sets its own time-reckoning - the header's only time content being its 'Hainish Cycle 93, Ekumenical Year 1490-97' line. Wade says 'dictates' where the claim says 'keeps'.

verdicts.trueWording: "three different voices"; header introduced as "the second voice"
verdicts.note: Wade opens 'The opening is actually quite complex, because it involves three different voices', gives the chapter title as the first, then 'Then we hit the second voice:' followed by the archival header and 'This is a voice of ultimate authority' (the claim's quote, verbatim). She places the parade on page 2, so the three voices are the first page.

verdicts.trueWording: "From the Archives of Hain. Transcript of Ansible Document 01-01101-934-2-Gethen"
verdicts.note: Books on GIF review #280 fetched raw (200, 48,741 bytes); under the heading 'An opening excerpt' the header is reproduced with the archive name and the document number, and contains no finite verb before the following 'I'll make my report...' sentence.

verdicts.trueWording: "I'll make my report as if I told a story"
verdicts.note: Same excerpt, first sentence of the narration; the header above it names 'Report from Genly Ai, First Mobile on Gethen/Winter', tying the 'I' to Genly Ai. Narration of events begins only at 'It starts on the 44th diurnal...'.

verdicts.trueWording: "The story is not all mine, nor told by me alone"
verdicts.note: Same excerpt, opening the third paragraph, followed by 'Indeed I am not sure whose story it is' - both limbs (not wholly his, not told by him alone) on the page.

verdicts.trueWording: "It starts on the 44th diurnal of the Year 1491"
verdicts.note: Quote is verbatim in the Books on GIF excerpt, and within that sentence the ordinal day and numbered year do precede 'the planet Winter' and 'the nation of Karhide'. But the claim's absolute wording fails against the same page: the archival header above already names Hain, Ollul, Genly Ai and Gethen/Winter, and the preceding paragraph names the narrator's homeworld.
verdicts.unsupportedLimb: 'before naming any person or place' - the header on the same page already names Hain, Ollul, Genly Ai and Gethen/Winter

verdicts.trueWording: "It is always the Year One here" - seven words, present tense
verdicts.note: Same excerpt; the sentence stands alone between the dating sentence and 'Only the dating of every past and future year changes each New Year's Day', so it states the local custom. Word count is exactly seven, tense is simple present.
